title: Only say the word (Matthew 8:5–13)
hookLine: a Roman officer asks healing for his servant and says he isn't worthy to have Jesus under his roof

cards: If you've ever been to a Catholic Mass, you've heard today's story, even if you didn't know it. Just before Communion, the whole church says a line together, a line about a roof.
It comes from a Roman soldier: a centurion, an army officer, a foreigner serving the power that rules the land. He's used to giving orders. People step aside when he walks by.
And one day in Capernaum he comes up to a Jewish teacher from Nazareth and asks for help. Not for himself. For his servant, lying at home, paralyzed and suffering terribly.

teach.h: I AM NOT WORTHY. ONLY SAY THE WORD.
teach.b: Jesus answers at once: I will come and heal him. The officer stops him. In the Douay-Rheims: "Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed."
Then he explains, like a soldier: I'm a man under authority myself, with soldiers under me. I say to one, go, and he goes. To another, come, and he comes.
He knows how a word works when it comes from someone with authority. You don't have to walk across town. Just say it.
Matthew says Jesus marveled. The one who usually amazes the crowds is amazed himself. He turns to the crowd following him: "Amen I say to you, I have not found so great faith in Israel."
A foreigner, an officer of a foreign power, held up as the example. Then Jesus tells him: go, and as you have believed, so be it done to you. The servant is healed in that same hour.
Long ago, in Latin, the Mass borrowed this man's words for the moment before Communion, changing only one thing: instead of my servant, my soul.
Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed. The roof is now the person. A soldier's humble sentence has become the whole Church's.

how: At every Mass, just before Communion, the congregation says together a response adapted from the centurion's words, asking to be healed in soul.

games.why: “Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.”

practice: Let the soldier's sentence move through you slowly, I am not worthy, but only say the word, and hold both halves together for a few breaths: the first is honest, the second trusts.
If you go to Mass, listen next time for the whole room saying it at once. If you pray, you can say it now, quietly, for yourself or for someone you're worried about; if not, just let it sit.

wordCard.voice: centurion. A Roman officer who trusted a word alone could heal his servant, without Jesus ever entering his house.

orig.note: Latin: Lord, I am not worthy. The opening of the words said before Communion in the Latin Mass.

carryVoice: Your line: I am not worthy. Honest about yourself, and trusting anyway. See you at day forty.
